text: I can describe the Init, Invoke and Shutdown lifecycle and explain what survives between invocations and what doesn't.
I can explain why a traffic spike makes concurrency overshoot during cold starts and estimate it as rate × (cold start + duration).
I can turn requests per second and duration into required concurrency and pick a reserved-concurrency cap from a database's connection limit.
I can compute the break-even request rate between functions and an always-on fleet from GB-second and request prices.
I can name at least five workload traits that make FaaS a poor fit and propose the alternative for each.
